title: The Shelf Keeps Nothing

arc.title: The Cold Stone
arc.subtitle: a warm stone, already going cold

epigraph.text: Two gaps on a shelf are two gaps till a finger lays them together. After that they are an account, and an account wants a name. Keep your finger off the shelf.
epigraph.attribution: A saying of the loaf-shelves of Low Kiln

pov: Daniel Marchetti (Corin), close third-person past tense inside a ninety-four-to-one-hundred-day-old body carried everywhere; the old life colours the noticing (an exact count kept against a house that keeps it badly, the hand to the record before the hand to the person, an anatomy read perfectly and worth nothing) without a present-tense Chicago break or a \memory{} tag --- the old life stays offstage --- and there is no departure from his eyes, no Court, Waiting Room or collector interior

scenes.title: What the Fist Held
scenes.synopsis: One dated entry, Day 94, Seed 5, Fifthday, morning in the strips east of Low Kiln on the barley fields and back through the Clay Yard, the well and the Vail kiln-house at dusk. The seed is in the ground and the work of the planting is now the work of waiting: brooms go around what the sweep left, a woman pushes the bristles around a stone and looks at the ground a moment longer than the stone requires, and a fist that let seed out comes back empty with chaff in the creases. Nobody puts a figure to the hands, the strips or the seed. The boy, ninety-four days old and carried at the edge, keeps the count exactly while the house keeps its days badly in loaves pushed along a shelf, glances at the clay jar and a space at the row's end nobody calls a number. He reads the emptied fist the way he once read a chart closed with a neat line and a signature at the foot, and the reading is exact and buys nothing. Sella gives the broom its instruction before anybody and never to the basket, says the house where another woman says I, and tells the fire it is the thaw; the widow's mark is touched at no hour because a strip, a broom, a basket, a well and a bed are not openings. The new finer grey in the Vail corner lies unswept beside the clean dark line; the carried fire keeps four, four and a gap under blind ash and the back of a broken pot, its payer unnamed for ninety-four days; one brown-edged crust lies stiff in the fold with the empty place beside it still unnamed and no third. Change: the planting has become worked ground that asks to be counted and nobody counts it, so the boy's exactness has no object left but its own number. Advances T071/T072 (94), T077, T058/T079, T060/T086, T009/T013/T092, T088. Withheld: no figure for hands, strips or seed, no name for the empty place, no seventh hearing, no ending.

scenes.title: The Shelf Keeps Nothing
scenes.synopsis: One dated entry, Day 95, Seed 6, Sixthday, morning and midday in the Vail kiln-house at the loaf shelf and the clay jar, dusk under the roof. Meaningful change: the loaf row on the house's shelf now stands with two empty places where one used to stand --- another loaf's worth has gone off the board without anybody marking it, beside the old space at the row's end that nobody calls a number --- and nobody names either gap or lays either beside the empty place at the boy's ear. A woman reaching for the shelf moves her hand over the new gap and goes on with the pot; Sella moves her lips along the row, glances at the clay jar and gives the instruction to the pot and the fire and never to the basket, saying the house. The boy sets the new gap on the shelf and the empty place in the fold on two places that do not touch and writes no cause across the space between them; he has learned what three likenesses in a row will do to a man who wants an answer, and here are two absences in two rooms with nobody putting a hand to either. He wants the number of his days spoken by somebody who would know what it counted and gets none. Tarn's knife is on its sill with six counted and the seventh nearly gone and still held; the carried fire misses its fifth breath and the new grey is unswept and called the thaw. Advances T060/T086 (the second empty place planted, held apart), T009/T013/T092, T071/T072 (95), T058/T079, T088, T036. Plant for the later day a house is left where it is and still kept and for the gift entered on no slate; do not solve, name or join the two absences now. Withheld: no cause, no joining of the two places, no third crust, no opening, no ending.

scenes.title: The Bite That Holds
scenes.synopsis: One dated entry, Day 96, Seed 7, Seventhday, before light through midday in the Vail wheel-shed and its damper, in the Clay Yard and under the Vail roof at dusk. Jorra comes through the finger's-width-open door with fine grey slate dust worked into both forearms past the bend of his little finger, not the bone-coloured slip of the wheel; men came in since first light and spoke low in the back room and he gives the house no name for them. The broken birth-slates stay under the lowest rack, gone around as wide as a pail of hot water set where a child might knock it and entered by nobody. He speaks to the wheel before anyone --- it does not care whose hands, only if they are steady --- tells a pot it will do, knows the full note of a Vail pot before it leaves the wheel and will not say so before a kiln-master from High Kiln. When Sella has not finished telling him the fire is low, his bent finger goes into the damper ahead of her sentence, the cold iron taking the cold out of his fingertip, so the end of her instruction arrives at the pot and the household straightens around his silence the way cloth straightens when a weight is lifted. He reads the damper as any iron that stops a thing from running: the same bite that keeps a vessel whole can take the hand off a man, and no word in Grathic holds both mercies; he keeps the reading to himself, an anatomy of the house's danger exact and worth nothing. Tarn takes the broom only after Sella has given it its instruction, goes over the collector's road without turning along it, and keeps the seventh year pressed and held with six counted in a mark his thumb has worn almost flat; to the kindling, Six counted. The next I don't count. He was sent for a collector once in the Long Cold, came back at the frozen ford and told the house it had been done, and keeps that sentence where he keeps the seventh year. A vessel gives its note past the door and his head does not turn and he does not name the sound; the boy does not call it a seventh hearing and the two ears keep their equality under one roof with the loan uncalled. He's not Vail stays sealed and the promise of the foundling's name to the men who burn slates is neither given nor withdrawn. Advances T035/T031, T062 (read, filed, not paid), T065/T095, T036/T076, T061/T082, T058/T079, T071/T072 (96). Withheld: no name for the men, no slate examined, no name given, no spending of the seventh year, no seventh hearing, no ending.

scenes.title: Twice Beneath the Grey
scenes.synopsis: One dated entry, Day 97, Seed 8, Eighthday, dawn market through afternoon at the Fishstairs below the north bridge; a short passage three doors down in House Silt; dusk under the Vail roof. Sella sets the basket at the edge of the fish-trade shade where no slate lies and gives the instruction to the wool and the water, never to the basket. Mira Silt works the eels with pale slime dried on her sleeves, silt in the hollow of her neck and her head held where the top of her left ear had been, her small smile kept like a door on the latch; asked whether the run will be thin she answers with her own question and answer, Thin? Who's to say thin? It comes when it comes. Ask the river, and moves eel-bones against her thumb while deciding whether to lie. When a buyer names a figure her thumb goes under her apron to the grey cord and stays; shifting a creel shows the second cord twisted twice beneath it, never carried upriver to Nine Pots or lifted at a door, neither knot counted and the knot for the thin child upriver untouched. Her board lies beside Orra's knot-string and does not touch it; Orra stays offstage watching and gets no answer. The steps come back four, four and a landing a hand's breadth out of line that a whole market walks carefully over without a fall; the soft-cuffed clerk still sits with his cuff gone grey from washing and his slate to his forearm for a measure nobody called, hand to slate before eyes to stalls, filed apart from Marra, the Drawing collector and the Court-table clerk, with no sixth sighting of the neat dark hand. Three doors down Alda Reed lays her birth-slates writing-down before she turns to the fold, crosses two fingers at the red edge of the birth-flower before she knows it and covers the sign with a dead woman's date; Warm and breathing, that's all I've set down, exact and not true; her hand goes once to the little tin in her bodice without opening it and her sixth slate stays face-down toward a floorboard, six pages unread and no seventh written. Above the abandoned board-bed the round pewter tin keeps its pale fold and thumb-bright rub unopened; two private records in two materials stand apart in one room, read by nobody and carried to no door. The boy sets Mira's not-looking, a keeping, in a place that does not touch the pricing he saw at the strips. Advances T059/T025/T024, T023/T089 (carried, not paid again), T090/T080, T007/T008/T073, T058/T079, T071/T072 (97). Withheld: no knot counted, no door knocked at Nine Pots, no sixth sighting, no tin opened, no seventh page, no ending.

scenes.title: A Foot the Water Left
scenes.synopsis: One dated entry, Day 98, Seed 9, Ninthday, morning below the sill and midday at the edge of the Fishstairs market, dusk under the Vail roof. Below the sill a child who waded when the water went comes up with a foot that stayed dark and cold after the wool went round it; a woman calls it the cold and the yard calls the water weather, so the two facts still never meet. The boy reads the extremity going before the core and the afterdrop waiting on the far side of a warming nobody will perform, knows the exact order of it and can put no hand two paces out; the reading works perfectly and is worth nothing, and the foot stays uncured, uncaused and unnamed. At the market's edge a small foundling in cast-offs worn like a uniform, a gap where a front tooth had been and a green sliver of lead-glaze on a string at his throat, is glimpsed unnamed in the narration: when a pot is set down his head goes toward it a half-beat after the boy's, after the knuckle and after the note, and he stops, rubs the sliver and cannot say why. He opens his mouth on the tail of a kiln-hand's sentence and does not finish it; no new loaf passes, no slate is seen and no secret changes hands that a slate could read, while the warm loaf from the man from Slate Row on Silt 16 goes on gathering interest in an account the child cannot read. The boy files the delay on a place of its own --- after the knock, not before, not a hearing and not a seventh --- and keeps his own turning beside it without letting the two touch; he is not Marra, not the Fishstairs clerk and not the Court-table clerk. No vessel gives a seventh hearing. Advances T093/T094/T096, T033/T034, T061/T082, T058/T079, T071/T072 (98). Withheld: no silt-leach, no cause, no cure, no recognition, no sale paid, no betrayal landed, no seventh hearing, no ending.

scenes.title: One in Twelve, Twice
scenes.synopsis: One dated entry, Day 99, Seed 10, Tenthday and Account-day, morning through afternoon at the Cross and a short turn at the Fishstairs, dusk under the Vail roof. Sella sets the basket in the moot-post's shade and carries it at a half-pace from every open slate. Berr Clay comes to the block with the red wool cord of his office folded under his coat and the green of tasted glaze at one corner of his mouth, wipes his thumb twice before touching nothing, reads one in twelve twice over the basket as the notice says, calls the levy and says it is not called by him, passes a finger over the figure and goes off toward High Kiln with the box locked and the true subtraction unspoken, believing he has done a kindness. A figure read aloud is not the figure paid; the number for what the planting will cost goes from a fist to a mouth to a shoulder and arrives nowhere. The bell goes four, four and a gap over the market and nobody crosses himself; Sella does not look into the basket and says nothing about what was read over it. A man from Slate Row whose name is on no roll, with soft hands of a man who sits at a table and the patient face of a man who can wait in a doorway, is glimpsed handing a figure to a slate; he is filed apart from Marra, the Drawing collector with grey fingers, the Court-table clerk and the soft-cuffed Fishstairs clerk, neither joined to the child nor to the loaf and not called a sale. At the steps the soft-cuffed clerk is still set for a measure nobody called, hand to slate before eyes to stalls; no sixth sighting of the neat dark hand comes. The boy is ninety-nine days old and nobody has told him so, and the figure that went over him twice did not know his number. Advances T015/T041/T047/T077/T078, T090/T080, T033/T080 (the soft hands, filed apart), T071/T072 (99), T058/T079, T061/T082. Withheld: no true subtraction spoken, no box opened, no figure for the planting, no joining of the soft hands to the loaf, no sixth sighting, no ending.

scenes.title: One Hundred
scenes.synopsis: One dated entry, Day 100, Seed 11, Firstday, morning in the Clay Yard and the strips, afternoon under the Vail kiln-house roof, dusk on the bed under the roof. The boy is one hundred days old, three months and ten days, and nobody marks it, names it or gives him a figure for it; the count he has kept exactly since the first day reaches a round number that the house cannot keep and does not try to. The seed stands in the strips and the yard goes around the brown skin holding a boot-print, the clean dark line, the new finer grey and the space under the lowest rack with a broom and a glance and no figure spoken; the loaf shelf keeps its two unnamed gaps and the fold keeps its one stiff crust and its one unnamed empty place, in two rooms that do not touch. Under the roof the private file is checked the way a man checks instruments laid out on a towel and is unchanged: six hearings of the full note stay six beside and never among, five from four sources and the sixth out of a person, with no seventh; three near-full answers stand on their tray advanced and not paid; the three intervals stay on another; the word forty is unspoken with the readable shape of the double turn beside it and the weight of a thumb apart from both; four low things keep their four places with the river's note of water going over water a fifth thing and not a hearing; the two tellings of the shut counting room stay on their tray joined to no kiln with likeness and difference kept; the loan that can hear stays uncalled. The carried fire keeps four, four and a gap under blind ash and the back of a broken pot, its payer unnamed for a hundred days; Sella sets him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without looking at his face and leaves the thread frozen; the widow's mark is untouched because a strip, a shelf, a bed and a door are not openings. The door stands a finger's width open with the river's low muttered note from the Ilm coming through the gap, nearer at the going of the water than at its coming, and the fire's four, four and a gap coming through the floor, the two sounds in two separate places as for a hundred days. His hand outside the wool goes up an inch toward the note of water going over water and comes down. Nothing joined, paid, explained or ended; the count stands at one hundred, unspent. Advances T071/T072 (100, a milestone kept, not paid), T086/T060, T092/T009/T013, T061/T082, T088, T058/T079, T093/T094. Withheld: no spoken number, no joining of the two gaps, no seventh hearing, no sixth sighting, no spending of the seventh year, no ending.
